conditional_hypotheses.decisive_uncertainty: Whether the block is receptor-responsive and causal, or a consequence of seizures, or of the neuron's own signal being absent (the pro-myelinating-class row asks the premise from the signal side). The agent also has systemic actions that oppose the glycaemia need; an effect on seizure threshold was not looked up. IT22: the seizure-threshold question is now looked up and is mixed, not closed.
conditional_hypotheses.evidence_available: WWOX-system: precursor cells increased and mature oligodendrocytes decreased after neuron-restricted WWOX deletion, restored by neuronal add-back (IT14), with the add-back window early; the myelin deficit is partly prevented when WWOX is restored in neurons in the neonatal window. Outside WWOX: in a mouse model of a thyroid-hormone-uptake defect, a thyromimetic normalised myelination and interneuron differentiation only when started in the first three postnatal weeks (abstract-level reading). No myelin compound has been given to a WWOX system, and another myelin compound already has a negative developmental-myelination result in this module. IT22 P6 (partial full text of the two human trials of the molecule in a hormone-entry defect; mouse rescue; OPC literature at abstract level): the human precedent has no neurodevelopmental endpoint; the mouse rescue works only in postnatal weeks 1-3 and the effective dose suppressed the thyroid axis; precursor cells express receptor-alpha rather than receptor-beta in rodents (abstract level), so a receptor-beta-leaning liver-directed agent is an isoform control, not a candidate; seizure evidence is mixed (worsening in 3 patients with prior seizures; hyperthyroid rats more seizure-prone). [IT36] The early-window result is now read at partial full text; a hormone-deprived brain also shows low parvalbumin counts; the receptor-isoform sentence of the source is contested and is not carried.

conditional_hypotheses.next_test: Seizure-free neuron plus precursor co-culture with wild-type and WWOX-deficient neurons: first measure T3 and T4 in the complete co-culture and spheroid media (B27 and N2 are present and the B27 formulation can carry T3), then the agonist against vehicle, with the native hormone as the primary receptor comparator and a transport-independent agonist as the second comparator; a depleted-medium arm only when a defined medium exists and its effect on the neurons is checked; a null agonist result in complete medium may be a ceiling effect, with a receptor-isoform-selective control; read precursor and mature-cell counts. Correction in both genotypes means non-specific maturation; correction only in the deficient condition opens a pre-onset in vivo question; no change closes the route. It enters at rank 6, below the ten-row line and behind the lithium and GABA-T rows (which carry a risk flag and human clinical reports and are not displaced by conditional probes), because the test is cell-level and inexpensive and an approved molecule exists for any later step, not because it is new: the precedent comes from a hormone-uptake defect in another disease and does not transfer by itself, and it sits below the two premise measurements (the dichloroacetate and NRF2 rows).

conditional_hypotheses.decisive_uncertainty: Whether the same step clears the Q230P-class protein in neural cells, and whether spared protein is functional (the degron and the GSK3B docking site may be one conformational event, giving a stable but inert protein). HSC70 also folds proteins, so blocking it may harm instead of help; the mirrored harm arm is carried as a second conditional arm. IT22: the weakest link is the substrate itself: no WWOX missense protein is shown above the assay floor, so gate 0 is a KO-controlled blot for the protein (the G372R line first).
conditional_hypotheses.evidence_available: WWOX-system: the Q230P class shows no protein band with a normal transcript; a different missense (P252A) over-expressed in non-neural cells is cleared faster and restored by lysosomal inhibitors but not by a proteasome inhibitor. Compound side: a curated inhibitor action on HSPA8 exists; the one reference reports impaired HSC70 refolding and lower lysosomal degradation in lupus-mouse B cells (abstract-level reading). Nothing shows that the route and the allele are the same. IT22 P6: the peptide's measured binding is micromolar (7.32 uM by surface plasmon resonance), refolding is inhibited at 40 uM, and its own paper reads its action as flux slowing like a lysosomal-acidification inhibitor; the one measured rescue of a WWOX missense is over-expressed P252A in non-neural cells.

IT22 P6 correction: the reference that carried the opposite sign used a different EZH2-blocking agent and siRNA, not the probe; in microglia the cytokines did not change and the rise came through medium from EZH2-suppressed tumour cells. Separate hazard: Ezh2 loss delays oligodendrocyte differentiation and Ezh1 compensates (mouse), so dual EZH1/EZH2 blockers are the highest-risk members. The arm is now reached from two different WWOX observations (glial cytokines and NRF2 tone), but through shared network edges, so it is not independent support.

conditional_hypotheses.decisive_uncertainty: Whether catalytic inhibition reproduces knockdown at SLC2A1 in a human neural cell: knockdown is not catalytic inhibition when the enzyme acts mostly as a scaffold. The premise is refuted if a catalytic-dead rescue restores SLC2A1 like wild type, if compound X leaves SLC2A1 unchanged while knockdown moves it and its cellular engagement of HDAC5 has been shown (without that, a null cannot separate scaffold function from non-engagement); a class-I-only inhibitor that reproduces the knockdown is ambiguous, because HDAC5 repression runs through HDAC3, and does not refute it alone; if inhibition raises SLC2A1 the lever inverts. Whether a change in SLC2A1 is favourable, compensatory or harmful in WWOX-deficient neural cells is itself unresolved, and a change in SLC2A1 is not a benefit. Potency of the broader HDAC compounds on HDAC5 cannot be compared until the methods of the three potency papers are readable (WO-29, data access blocked).
conditional_hypotheses.evidence_available: Edge: HDAC5 to SLC2A1 traces to one origin, human primary muscle cells, where HDAC5 knockdown reduced GLUT1 expression (PMID 22991226, abstract level); the one drug tested there was pan-HDAC and was reported for GLUT4 only. Class IIa enzymes have very low intrinsic activity on standard substrates and repress largely as scaffolds; in neurons the separating experiments exist for HDAC4, not HDAC5; cardiomyocyte data show catalytic activity mattering for HDAC5 with the opposite sign (inhibition raises the output). Compound side: Compound X identity confirmed by full InChIKey (CHEMBL3110004); ChEMBL values from one paper, HDAC4 130, HDAC5 80, HDAC7 40, HDAC9 20 nM, in a recombinant catalytic-domain assay, cross-paper values vary and whether each was measured or quoted was not checked; whether compound X engages HDAC5 in cells at the cited exposures is not determined. Attribution gap of the pan-class comparator in this thread: vorinostat is held on main_target_weak_attribution (HDAC5 Ki 3600 against HDAC1 1.3 nM, fold 2769.2), so an effect of that compound would read as class I. Counter-premise carried in the generator: class I and pan-HDAC inhibition are signed adverse for oligodendrocyte maturation; for class IIa the CNS sign is unknown, the only myelin datum is a peripheral Schwann-cell double mutant of Hdac4 and Hdac5 (PMID 29472387, partial full text), and WWOX neuron-deleted mice are hypomyelinated. WWOX-system: HDAC5 mRNA nominally lower and SLC2A1 nominally higher in the P47T mouse, an mRNA association only; the human organoid shows SLC2A1 higher on transcript. IT32 reading of neural precedents: a catalytic-domain mutant of HDAC5 (two cysteines) lost deacetylase activity in vitro and abolished the effect of nuclear HDAC5 on one transcript and on a behaviour in rat nucleus accumbens (PMID 39923817, full text; no SLC2A1 or glucose readout, and loss of binding to another factor is not excluded), so the earlier statement that no neural catalytic arm exists is out of date; a catalytic-site mutant of the paralog HDAC4 rescued survival like the wild type in mouse cortical neurons (PMID 23141539); an inhibitor matched knockdown on neurite growth in neural cells but was inert where knockdown of HDAC7 acted (PMID 31572723; PMID 41962726, abstract only). Catalytic dependence is therefore specific to paralog, cell type and output. IT32 action-level reading (NB-3b): the premise source tested knockdown only, that is protein amount, and its pan-inhibitor arm names no GLUT1 result (abstract level); results for the paralog HDAC4 on GLUT1 go in both directions in non-neural cells; the direction of SLC2A1 in WWOX-deficient systems differs between the organoid, mouse brain and shWWOX neural cells, and no source reads SLC2A1 after HDAC5 manipulation in a neural cell. [IT36] the abstract reports GLUT4 promoter activity and no GLUT1 promoter result; sign is paralogue- and tissue-dependent; HDAC4 results are never carried to HDAC5. [IT36] HDAC5 and HIF-1alpha: knockdown or inhibition lowers hypoxic HIF-1alpha and GLUT1/CA9 mRNA in human cancer cell lines through a cytosolic, catalytic route (PMID 26061431, full text); association with the inhibitory domain raises transactivation without stabilisation (PMID 19071119, abstract); HDAC5 silencing lowers HIF1A in an epilepsy-model neuron (PMID 34021541); opposite-sign reports exist (abstracts). Scaffold and catalytic readings are both reported and the sign is context-dependent; HIF-1alpha is a candidate mediator of undetermined sign in neural cells; no therapeutic link in WWOX is shown. [IT39] Corrections carried from the repeat: the ketogenic paper, the MC1568 and Bdnf statement, the pooled SPR range, lithium specificity and the source type of ICP0 were each misstated in an external report; human primary muscle cells with HDAC5 knockdown show lower GLUT1 expression (opposite in sign to that report's table); a route through HDAC4, MEF2A and GLUT1 exists.
conditional_hypotheses.evidence_depth: Conditional hypothesis: the edge has one muscle origin read at abstract level and the compound side is compiled data; a catalytic-domain mutant of HDAC5 exists in rat neurons for other outputs (PMID 39923817) but none reads SLC2A1 in a human neural cell (no ranked unit, so no evaluation depth applies: this is not a depth of zero)

conditional_hypotheses.decisive_uncertainty: Branch A, compensatory Ih: blocking it worsens or leaves bursts; weakened if bursts fall. Branch B, pro-excitatory Ih through the depolarised resting potential: blocking it lowers bursts at matched membrane potential; weakened if bursts do not fall. Branch C, bystander: no effect on bursts although sag falls; weakened by any burst change. The sag itself must first be shown to be Ih (sensitive to the blocker), and a blocker that shifts the resting potential acts on the premises of A and B at once. Branch D, added from an unguided expansion (IT35): the higher input resistance of the knockout and the heterozygote is the opposite of what a larger Ih alone would give (in a rat cortical dysplasia model reduced Ih came with a higher input resistance, reversed by an Ih blocker, PMID 21795624; there the resting potential is hyperpolarised, so it is not a mirror image), so a second or alternative change, such as loss of a resting potassium conductance (Kir, K2P or Kv7 channels), is a rival explanation; weakened if blocker-sensitive potassium currents do not differ.
conditional_hypotheses.evidence_available: WWOX-system, one preparation read in full and re-extracted (PMID 34634460, Table 1 and Figure 6): resting potential -79.25, -75.51, -73.62 mV and sag at a fixed -200 pA step 1.18, 2.04, 2.57 mV grade with gene dose, input resistance saturates at one allele, rebound is marked larger only in the knockout (the printed p cannot be reproduced from the Table 1 means and dispersion under stated assumptions), and bursts occur in 36 of 42 knockout, 4 of 23 heterozygote and 0 of 11 wild-type slices; the authors name control of the resting membrane potential as a factor underlying the hyperexcitability (the frequency-current slope does not differ once the curves are shifted to one step below rheobase; supplement not read) and cite discordant Ih-blocker precedents, including worsening of 4-AP events. Compound side: Ih-acting tools exist in the catalogue (a clinically used HCN blocker and several research blockers, identities resolved), found by the need search without naming any; their cellular potency in a cortical pyramidal neuron and their selectivity among HCN isoforms were not assessed here. No Ih-blocker experiment in a Wwox-deficient preparation is recorded in the entries read. [IT39] Ivabradine blocks sag and hyperpolarises cortical L5 and L6 neurons in normal rat slices, and injection into somatosensory cortex cut absence-seizure time by 96 percent against 40 percent in thalamic VB (abstract); the GAERS authors read Ih as not an adaptive response to spike-wave discharges (input resistance fell, resting potential and sag unchanged), which sits beside the discordant precedents.

conditional_hypotheses.next_test: In knockout, heterozygote and wild-type slices: sag, resting potential, input resistance, rebound and burst incidence before and after two Ih blockers of different chemotypes (the second so that an off-target action is not read as Ih), with a current-clamp step that matches the resting potential and the peak potential, with a smaller cell or immature membrane listed as its own candidate beside branch D, and a voltage-clamp read of the blocker-sensitive current in a subset of cells; animals, not cells, are the replicates. Branch D adds the potassium-current arm: the potassium currents sensitive to a Kv7 blocker and to a Kir-channel blocker in voltage clamp, and input resistance read with synaptic transmission blocked. [IT36] A first-generation Ih blocker at 50 uM is about 40 times its sodium-current IC50 in DRG neurons (age not stated); read a second chemotype and the blocker-sensitive current in voltage clamp; nickel/Z944 and Kv7 arms separate.

deepened_cases.compound_action: GluN2B negative allosteric modulators at the ifenprodil site: ifenprodil and Ro 25-6981 as tools, radiprodil as clinical-stage comparator
deepened_cases.counter_evidence: A steeper-than-linear burst fall is not a valid discriminator alone (burst generation is threshold-like).

deepened_cases.pharmacology_limits: Ifenprodil inhibition is incomplete and triheteromers are partly inhibited; conditions differ between the two compounds; radiprodil has only complex-level values (not determinable).

further_investigations.decisive_uncertainty: Which of the six layers moves, per animal. A lower transcript does not show fewer cells, lower activity or less inhibition; an absent change in GSE158684 is not evidence of no change; the oligodendrocyte-lineage shift could be consequence or cause of an excitation-inhibition change and the data cannot say which. Whether any parvalbumin-cell change is a deficit, a compensation or a delayed maturation is unresolved, so the need direction stays unresolved and no lever sign is derived. Whether recombination reaches parvalbumin cells, and glia, in this deletion is not known from any source read, and a reporter measured in another context does not measure the excision of Wwox in parvalbumin cells. [IT36] Whether the parvalbumin deficit and the maturation block of the myelin model share a cause is open.
further_investigations.evidence_available: WWOX-system, transcript: a lower Pvalb transcript in the neuron-targeted deletion in bulk hippocampus (log2 -1.70, GSE158681 S contrast, as quoted in IT13b) and about half that size in the nuclear data (GSE158684: Pvalb 70 against 37 UMI in 3182 against 2920 nuclei; nuclei Pvalb share ratio 0.59). GSE158684 holds one pooled library per arm (library and animal index absent; the paper states n = 1 per arm), so nuclei are not biological replicates and the GSM records of the series are not independent experiments; PV-class nuclei number 12 to 19 per arm under the producer rules, the independent recompute disagrees on the specific counts, and PV composition and Pvalb per cell are undecidable under every rule tried. Kcnc1 is lower in inhibitory nuclei (one pool, not a replicate result). Immature-neuron markers (Sox11, Dcx, Igfbpl1) are higher in knockout neurons in direction; the larger composition change is oligodendrocyte-class nuclei, about 3- to 5-fold fewer. Wwox also falls in glia-called nuclei, unexplained. Protein and function, from the need file: PV-positive counts reduced by 44 percent in the whole hippocampus of a systemic constitutive knockout (PMID 30290271) and spontaneous inhibitory current amplitude more than halved in layer II/III pyramidal neurons of the neuron-specific knockout (PMID 34634460; unit of the KS test not declared; the size of the p values is compatible with events and not with one value per cell). Raw reads of the eight snRNA experiments (SRX9206272 to SRX9206279) carried NCBI status hup on 2026-10-31. A public conference abstract (poster 014, Curing the Epilepsies 2026 programme, NINDS; the whole abstract was read, abstract level) describes a programme that combines genetic mouse models, in vivo electrophysiology, ex vivo slice recordings, cell type-specific manipulations and targeted pharmacological modulation of neuronal activity in WWOX deficiency, and names parvalbumin interneurons as the population of interest; it reports no quantitative result, no molecule, no rescue and no target. IT33 reading of the glial signal (NB-4 pilot, independently audited): the deletion is neuron-targeted by design (Synapsin-Cre) and a lower Wwox transcript also appears in glia-annotated nuclei of one pool (oligodendrocyte-called 193 to 1 UMI, astrocyte-called 156 to 9: very small counts on the deleted side, one pool per arm, so a count of cells or a statement of glial loss is not supported); the readings are several and not exclusive (lower transcript in the annotated class, class definition and detectability, ambient RNA, recombination beyond the expected cells, a change of state or composition), and none is isolated. Two abstract-level sources describe the Synapsin-Cre line: germline recombination through male carriers (PMID 16419044) and non-cell-autonomous astrogliosis after a neuronal deletion of another gene (PMID 11297510); neither shows or excludes recombination in glia or in parvalbumin cells of this deletion. IT33 verified delta (independent audit, 19 of 21 rows supported, two narrowed): an independent characterisation of the same Cre line with an X-linked Mecp2 reporter in adult male mice (PMID 35966957, full text without the figures) found reporter activation in 36 percent of NeuN-high brain nuclei, incomplete in cortex and minimal in cerebellum, and could not exclude activity in a subset of glia; the reporter, locus, age and cross differ from the Wwox deletion, so these percentages are not carried to the excision of Wwox or to parvalbumin cells; in the Wwox paper's P17 cortical field WWOX is retained in some NeuN-positive cells, and in one callosal field in some CC1-positive cells of the knockout; no tdTomato panel was found in the surfaces read. [IT36] no WWOX bridge to the perineuronal-net matrix found (PubMed 0 hits; Europe PMC titles only); the only lead (HYAL2/WWOX complex) concerns neuronal death, not nets. [IT36] The mean of the declared inhibitory current amplitude comes from events of 9 to 14 cells and 5 to 7 animals; no animal-level statistic is given for current amplitudes; 10 of 18 reported KS p values lie below the one-value-per-cell floor and 8 do not, and no contradiction of the paper is asserted. [IT39] Model identity of the conditional line is Synapsin-Cre; a statement of zero hits for parvalbumin loss is wrong (about 44 percent fewer PV-positive cells in the 2-week full-knockout hippocampus); perineuronal-net counter-evidence exists and two explanations of an external report are mutually inconsistent.

further_investigations.decisive_uncertainty: Driver, marker or consequence. If the MYC difference vanishes within cell-cycle and potency strata it is a marker and this observation alone justifies no lever; if genetic lowering of MYC moves the progenitor shift it is a driver, and the timing of any window is a separate question, not assumed to be prenatal only. MYC dose is two-sided in cortex and the record holds no safe pharmacological formulation for a developing compartment. Raised MYC cannot be called harmful and lowering it cannot be called therapeutic on this evidence; a MYC-directed lever carries an unmeasured risk in a developing compartment.
further_investigations.evidence_available: WWOX-system, one organoid study (PMID 42397075): MYC is the most raised gene in knockout radial glia, which shift toward S and G2M; the fraction of SOX2-positive cells that are MYC-positive is raised in an engineered knockout and two patient-derived lines; one non-selective multi-kinase inhibitor reported to suppress Wnt and MYC lowers the SOX2-positive fraction in knockout organoids; neuron-promoter add-back raises deep-layer fractions. Transcript and cell fractions only: no protein, no manipulation of MYC itself. IT33 reading (NB-1, independently audited, corrections applied): no MYC-selective perturbation of a WWOX system was found in the routes searched, the one non-selective perturbation being the multi-kinase inhibitor inside the same study; the only model in which lowering MYC changes a progenitor maturation phenotype is a human progenitor system with a different upstream lesion (one donor line), so the evidence for a driver role is transferred, not WWOX evidence; elsewhere MYC is not simply a maintenance factor (in some models lowering shrinks or redirects the progenitor pool); the SCAR12-class line shows MYC up with a wild-type-like radial-glia fraction; a WWOX-to-MYC relation is known only outside the brain; in the same study MYC protein is high while MYC binding at early-neuron gene promoters is lost in knockout neural stem cells.
further_investigations.evidence_depth: Premise measurement: the MYC rise is observed in one organoid study; its role is not measured. (no ranked unit, so no evaluation depth applies: this is not a depth of zero)

further_investigations.next_test: In WWOX-deficient and corrected isogenic organoids or radial-glia cultures: compare MYC within cell-cycle phase strata, then lower MYC by a genetic route with a second construct and read the progenitor fractions and the cell-cycle phase. No compound is needed for this step. Refinement from NB-1: lowering is graded and MYC-specific (not MYCN or MYCL unless measured), in two windows (radial-glia phase; neuron stage only), reading absolute counts of SOX2-, NEUN-, CTIP2- and SATB2-positive cells, cell death, glia and MYCN, in factorial design against restoring cell-cycle timing without touching MYC; the reading is wrong if markers do not move, the pool shrinks, glia rise, or the same lowering in the corrected line gives the same shift. [IT39 dream] In the same lines, read the HIF and glycolytic target genes beside the neuronal genes, and add a HIF1A or EPAS1 knockdown arm for the glycolytic readout: a MYC to HIF1A edge exists at database level (sign context-dependent) and HIF-axis data exist in WWOX cells (non-neural), so the MYC change could act on glycolysis, be reached from it, or follow a shared maturation or composition change; the measurement separates these only if each side is perturbed and the other read, in both directions and in time order: an unchanged readout after one perturbation shows that the first factor is not needed for that readout, not a causal direction (exploratory, no compound).

investigations.evidence_available: WWOX-system, read beyond the abstract: the high-dose arm reaches a survival plateau to day 300 and lowers spike-wave discharges to a wild-type-indistinguishable level; weight is ordered against wild type and the untreated knockout (equal to the high dose at P30 only), and glycaemia is NOT shown to be prevented: at P10 the treated arms are not significantly different from the untreated knockout (high dose about 113, low dose about 105, untreated knockout about 95; Figure 3E, card C04 DR-AAV-GLU10-HD and DR-AAV-GLU10-LD), at P20 the untreated-knockout comparator is absent because those animals are dead (Figure 3F, DR-AAV-GLU20-LD and DR-AAV-GLU20-HD, direction UNKNOWN) and the P20 result is dose-graded against wild type only, and by P30 the dose separation has closed (Figure 3G); the paper's own text states that both doses partially corrected hypoglycaemia, while the panel does not support it (card C04 records this: the treated arms are not significantly different from the untreated knockout at P10); the glucose result depends on age, dose and comparison, and a non-significant difference at P10 is not evidence of no benefit. Every treated arm was injected in the stated neonatal window.

investigations.next_test: One added arm of the published design with injection after the first recorded spike-wave discharge, same endpoints, untreated same-genotype comparator kept. Worded per endpoint class: measure the restoration actually achieved at the age of treatment and its regional distribution, because the one comparable later-age failure in a short-lived null was left uninterpretable by that missing measurement; carry a within-animal pre-treatment recording, a treated wild-type or heterozygote arm, growth and glycaemia as primary endpoints (growth failed even with pre-onset treatment in the closest analogue), and follow-up long enough to see decay. Quantified myelin sheath structure (g-ratio or electron microscopy, not marker intensity) is the discriminating endpoint for a neuron-driven lesion: white-matter abnormality has been reversed after a documented onset only in glial or metabolic lesions, and sheath structure after onset has been reported only in a metabolic oligodendrocyte-enzyme lesion (G-ratio by electron microscopy, one source) and not in any neuron-driven lesion. Spike-wave rate is the confirmatory endpoint and its external precedent (not WWOX evidence) is split, so pair it with a rhythm or power-spectrum measure; interneuron number as well as excitability, because no source measured number.

investigations.decisive_uncertainty: Whether the carded effect is a T-type effect at all, which isoform carries it, and whether it is genotype-dependent. Whether the two agents really differ in isoform reach at the concentrations used is itself unmeasured. The same effect from two compounds is compatible with a common target (the T-type class) and does not by itself weaken the T-type attribution; it only fails to discriminate isoforms. What would weaken the attribution is no effect of either agent at on-target exposure, an effect that tracks off-target activity rather than T-type potency, or an equal effect in wild type (no genotype dependence). [IT36] Z944 was measured on Cav3.2 only in the source read (human clone, HEK293T, whole cell); Cav3.1 and Cav3.3 values and mouse brain exposure are not obtained; the blocker class has not discriminated between isoforms.

investigations.evidence_available: Clinical reports only. Children counted once across 14 reports: 36 to 38 exposed to at least one of vigabatrin, hormonal therapy, ketogenic diet or cannabidiol (partial full-text depth in 11 reports, one source at abstract level). Both a symptomatic and a developmental outcome are recorded for 6. In 4 of them, a partial or transient improvement came with no developmental progress recorded; in 2, neither moved. No sustained, instrumented response is recorded, and no developmental gain follows any of the four classes. Vigabatrin: 5 children with both endpoints in 4 reports (4 discordant, 1 concordant non-response); these are not independent of the other classes, since three of the five also supply them and all five were on co-therapy. Children with both endpoints, by class, of those exposed: hormonal 3 of 11; ketogenic diet 2 of 12; cannabidiol 1 of 7. Counts only, no percentage (n below 10). Developmental statements are clinical narratives without a scale. A brain-imaging safety signal is recorded beside them in two children (abstract level, a report selected for the finding), so it is not a frequency. No WWOX child is recorded with a developmental gain after a symptomatic improvement. Four children in three reports (two of them in one report) had a partial, transient or clinically-defined improvement with development not progressing; two had neither. That is what the baseline in other genetic and structural early-onset encephalopathies predicts (a responder with poor development is the majority outcome in infantile spasms and near-universal in genetic strata), so it is not by itself a WWOX-specific feature. The comparison holds only as a binary: the baseline uses standardised scores with a cut, every WWOX developmental statement is a clinician narrative, and no WWOX child had a sustained, instrumented response. Non-WWOX DEE baseline (batch_sci_20261105 a2_baseline; not WWOX evidence): in a prospective IESS cohort read at partial full-text depth, 72 percent of responders (126 of 175, computed from its Table 1) were below the developmental cut at 3 years, and no genetic-aetiology child reached a favourable outcome (0 of 49, a count over all genetic-aetiology children, not a responder rate). In two randomised IESS trials (abstract level), arms that raised early spasm cessation by 15 to 19 points showed no demonstrated developmental difference, with about one chance in four of detecting the difference that full mediation would predict. In TSC, two randomised trials of pre-onset prevention changed seizure endpoints without changing development to 36 months; they test prevention before onset, not response after onset. The person-level association (ICISS, abstract level: 15.9 VABS points higher with early cessation) is carried by unknown aetiology and a normal first neurological examination. [IT36] the 2024 vigabatrin case: developmental statements uninstrumented, stall from spasm onset before drug; seizure-free at home while video-EEG still showed events. [IT39] The transfer from KCNQ2 and TSC is analogy; genotype stratification is established for mortality only; lithium is not the only existing-drug node (ethosuximide was also tested).

investigations_context.ceiling_rule: risk-flagged and human-report rows are not displaced by conditional probes
investigations_context.curation: Positions are curated judgements written by research agents (rows of investigations_it20.tsv) and reviewed one by one. The code validates them (complete fields, closed vocabularies, contiguous ranks, existing need and unit, no dose, no absence claim, no conditional hypothesis called qualified) and computes no position. Ceiling rule: the published list carries at most ten rows; a row that carries a risk flag (direction state opposed_risk) or real human clinical reports is never placed below the line by displacement from a conditional probe, which goes below the line instead (whole ties are kept together); a row below the line stays in the table with its reason and is not judged unpromising.

informative_negatives.detail_full: Curated mechanism rows in ChEMBL list inhibition of both IMPA1 and GSK3A/B for lithium; the sign argument rests on three abstract-level references. The null/wild-type panels (N 6 vs 7 and 12 vs 8) show a lithium effect of about the size of the difference between the lithium and ethosuximide null controls.
informative_negatives.reason: The documented consequence of inhibiting this enzyme in rodents is a pro-convulsant effect that inositol reverses, which predicts aggravation, not the protection seen; the protection also appears in wild-type littermates, so it is not specific to WWOX loss. The precedent is an analogy from another model (the drug together with low-dose pilocarpine), not a measurement in the Wwox assay, so it disfavours the route and does not close the assay question; the same mouse paper also ran a pilocarpine model in Wwox mice, so the objection that the provocations differ is testable in the same system.
informative_negatives.reopen: Inositol add-back reverses the lithium effect in the Wwox-null assay (then the GSK3 attribution falls and the enzyme becomes a lever with an unexplained sign).
informative_negatives.ruled_out: Disfavoured, not ruled out (DISFAVOURED_BY_SIGN_PRECEDENT): that inositol monophosphatase inhibition contributes to the protection lithium gives in the Wwox seizure assay, or that this enzyme is a lever for it.
informative_negatives.subject_label: Lithium (carded): inhibition of inositol monophosphatase as the mediator of its seizure protection

informative_negatives.detail_full: Path B reached these five genes through 80 signed inhibitor family-gene pairs, none named in a need; evidence for the competence deficit is non-neural (murine B cell and cell lines).
informative_negatives.reason: No scenario in the record makes over-activity of this response the harmful process; if the response is protective and already reduced, an inhibitor aggravates it. It is held as a harm flag, not a lever. Competence of the response in post-mitotic WWOX-deficient neurons is unmeasured.
informative_negatives.reopen: A WWOX-deficient neural measurement showing over-active checkpoint signalling that harms the cell.
informative_negatives.ruled_out: That an inhibitor of the DNA-damage response is a lever for a WWOX-deficient developing brain.

informative_negatives.ruled_out: The chain as written: that this inhibitor lowers SLC2A1 by acting on HDAC5 in a WWOX-deficient neural cell.

it22_changes.text: A decision about one molecule no longer blocks every molecule that shares its target: it travels only as far as its own reason (the molecule's own potency or label stays with it; a refuted premise still closes the arm it belongs to). 69 proposals were blocked by the old rule; 24 stay closed (premise refuted), 45 are released to be judged on their own data, none promoted.

Potency is compared only between measures of the same type; unlike measures are kept side by side and never turned into an exclusion. 20 proposals blocked on weak target attribution became 5 (the verifier's lower-bound rule restored one); the cautious case (a pan-HDAC inhibitor 2,769-fold weaker at the listed target, same measure type) stays blocked.

Observations that no generator input carried now reach it: a new question on NRF2 tone (one organoid contrast, adjusted p above the deposit's own alpha, role unknown) produced 20 new conditional proposals (the axis itself was already a carded thread since IT10; the compound routes are new); a failed control (the second neural system's progenitor arm did not show WWOX lower) is attached to 71 proposals and a contested direction to 75 more, as carried limits (recorded in the output; removing their ordering term changes no hand-over); a cell-type marker set can no longer become a gene seed; a premise or class limit now travels wherever its edge or target appears in a chain, not only inside one cluster.

What did not change: the number of generated proposals from the old inputs (980, only selection changed), the absence of any qualified hypothesis, and the earlier retrospective result (WWOX seed identity not separable from matched random sets on the measured properties only).

Seven of eight new hand-overs were qualified on their own data and end inconclusive or conditional. Seven of the 16 hand-overs rest on one organoid deposit and six flip direction if the unknown role of their question flips; the main limit is not the number of candidates but missing measurements in a WWOX-deficient neural system.

IT23 tried six external capabilities on cases frozen beforehand (a knowledge graph, a network simulator, a protein-profile matrix, a signature search, disease-module discovery and a prediction model): none was adopted as a tool. One relation type became a carried limit: spontaneous seizure reports now appear as counter-evidence on 31 proposal rows and one hand-over, without moving any eligibility. The audit of the action table also found five suspect sign rows in LEGEND's own data. A simulation returned the assumed scenario, a profile matrix could not score the hand-over compounds and a signature search did not overlap with LEGEND's list: for these inputs the limit is the missing measurement of the cytokine axis and a larger qualified seed set, not the number of tools.

IT24 corrected and extended what the generator reads. After a source check, eight signed pairs (one compound on seven sirtuins and another on a caspase) were withheld: each rested on one review-table or trial-listing claim and no primary source supports a direction; no opposite sign was assigned, and none was the main link of any proposal. Chemical identity was recovered for 93 of the 115 rows that IT23 could not compare (89 firm), without merging by name; the comparison with a drug-signature search stays empty on 136 comparable rows. Splitting the calculation by target showed 32 conflicts between targets of one compound, almost all of them small, and 4 handed-over compounds with several favourable targets (two of them paralog pairs). New per-gene lists from public mouse data (a knock-in model and conditional deletions) are candidate pools, not findings. No position in this ranking changed, and none of these steps measures benefit or predictive accuracy.

limits: EXPERIMENTAL: a retrospective comparison on a small, deliberately non-random reference (32 selected pairs over 25 compounds; 17 determinate, 11 from a functional measurement and 6 from a class-level attribution); no general accuracy and no superiority of one path over another is claimed.

Pharmacological compatibility means only that a documented action has the direction the need states. It is not research priority, not evidence of benefit in WWOX deficiency, and says nothing about safety or about whether the need's direction is the beneficial one.
Unknown is not negative: the bounded search found nothing, which is a statement about the search, not about the compound.

An abstention keeps the row visible with its action and its reason; it removes a direction the source row cannot carry, and on this selection it also removed one direction the reference supports (bepridil at the T-type need): no field yet lets a sourced subunit-level measurement re-license it.

The reference side was built by one actor who had seen the earlier labels; the module side is machine-generated from committed code. 8 of the 17 determinate rows are independent of the module's construction sources; agreement on the others is not independent confirmation.

matching_pilot.research_despite_requirements: I requisiti di sviluppo sistemico sono sfavorevoli o sconosciuti, ma il passo 0 e il braccio genetico (KEAP1, NFE2L2) non usano il composto e rispondono alla domanda di ruolo per ogni leva Q5; il verdetto della sonda ex vivo è separato da quello dello sviluppo e non è annullato da esso.

matching_pilot.evidence_limit: Nessun composto è stato dato a un sistema WWOX; le osservazioni ACK1-WWOX vengono da cancro (prostata, fegato) a livello di abstract; i valori ChEMBL ripetuti sono valori di letteratura riportati fra articoli, non repliche. Nessuna scheda e nessuna voce ordinata: la voce N12 non ha scheda. Dasatinib non è selettivo per ACK1 (34 bersagli più forti in un documento di profilazione) e bosutinib non è un chemotipo indipendente; il dato di knockdown è una linea di carcinoma epatocellulare, un costrutto, stato stazionario (IT11 P2.4).
matching_pilot.generating_path: Percorso non da grafo: Q1 non ha via di grafo; la ricerca complementare dei regolatori della stabilità della proteina trova ACK1, che fosforila WWOX in Tyr287 con poliubiquitinazione e degradazione (cellule LNCaP, abstract) e il cui knockdown alza WWOX in linee di epatocarcinoma (solo la direzione, abstract).

ACK1 over-expression with an engineered activated kinase phosphorylates WWOX, predominantly at Tyr287, and is…
matching_pilot.refutation: Nessuna variazione di emivita o di livello di WWOX con l'inibitore o con il knockdown di TNK2 in cellule neurali o con variante; risposta a un solo inibitore (fuori bersaglio); nessuna proteina in Q230P; ACK1 non attivo nei neuroni; sensibilizzazione all'apoptosi con ACK1 inibita nei neuroni granulari cerebellari di ratto.
matching_pilot.research_despite_requirements: Presenza di proteina, esposizione nel SNC e tollerabilità sono sconosciute: non tolgono la domanda su cosa limiti l'emivita di WWOX in una cellula che ha una banda, misurabile in vitro con la regola di concordanza. La voce resta senza scheda finché non c'è il testo completo di Mahajan 2005.
matching_pilot.research_priority: Prima il testo completo di Mahajan 2005 e il dato sul destino della proteina; poi, se c'è proteina, il confronto dasatinib, bosutinib e knockdown di TNK2.
matching_pilot.research_question: Emivita (cicloesimide) e livello stazionario di WWOX con composto, knockdown di TNK2 come comparatore genetico, WWOX Tyr287Phe come controllo insensibile; regola di concordanza fra i due inibitori e il knockdown; lettura di funzione separata dalla quantità. Bracci distinti per chemotipo e bracci genetici (Tnk2-null, un secondo shRNA con mRNA di WWOX) come primo passo.
matching_pilot.supporting_evidence: Due sistemi tumorali indipendenti (prostata, fegato; solo abstract); inibitori catalogati con potenza nanomolare misurata su TNK2 (valori di letteratura riportati fra articoli, non repliche). Nessun dato in una cellula neurale o con variante.

selection_table.counter_evidence_statements: IT12 P2.2 figure audit (dated 2026-10-31, PMID 37275776 Fig 7B, image viewed): the stored statement that the GIRK2 crossings lie inside the therapeutic band is wrong on one clause. In oocytes the GIRK2 homomer activated by Gbeta-gamma is half-maximally inhibited at about 0.03 to 0.06 mM, about 4 to 8 times BELOW the shaded band (about 0.25 to 0.9 mM), while the brain-predominant GIRK1/2 plus Gbeta-gamma channel crosses at about 0.4 to 1 mM, inside it (partial block, about 20 to 60 percent). So a measured non-T-type target exists at labelled exposure, and the wording 'T-type potency is weak against the labelled range' is not the whole story: the ethosuximide result in the WWOX mouse (PTZ seizure score) cannot be attributed to T-type mediation. An oocyte datum, not a WWOX mechanism; the authors say neuronal GIRK2 homomer abundance is unknown. In a genetic absence model the relay-neuron T-type current is smaller than control and the burst-threshold difference follows Ih (PMID 24953239 Figs 5 and 6). No group or member evidence changes. | IT13 P3a (2026-10-31): ethosuximide's attribution to T-type channels is not supported by any measurement in Wwox tissue: the catalogue mechanism record lists T-type only, the source paper's own oocyte data show GIRK block near the labelled band (a GIRK route would predict the opposite sign; prior knowledge), the two PTZ-alone null cohorts of the figure differ by about the size of the drug effect, no interaction test, and P17 Cacna1g/h/Kcnj6 transcripts are inside the control-line background. The late-phase effect stays one experiment in one laboratory; the group is unchanged.

selection_table.counter_evidence_statements: IT12 P2.2 figure audit (dated 2026-10-31, PMID 37275776 Fig 7B, image viewed): the stored statement that the GIRK2 crossings lie inside the therapeutic band is wrong on one clause. In oocytes the GIRK2 homomer activated by Gbeta-gamma is half-maximally inhibited at about 0.03 to 0.06 mM, about 4 to 8 times BELOW the shaded band (about 0.25 to 0.9 mM), while the brain-predominant GIRK1/2 plus Gbeta-gamma channel crosses at about 0.4 to 1 mM, inside it (partial block, about 20 to 60 percent). So a measured non-T-type target exists at labelled exposure, and the wording 'T-type potency is weak against the labelled range' is not the whole story: the ethosuximide result in the WWOX mouse (PTZ seizure score) cannot be attributed to T-type mediation. An oocyte datum, not a WWOX mechanism; the authors say neuronal GIRK2 homomer abundance is unknown. In a genetic absence model the relay-neuron T-type current is smaller than control and the burst-threshold difference follows Ih (PMID 24953239 Figs 5 and 6). No group or member evidence changes. | IT13 P3a (2026-10-31): ethosuximide's attribution to T-type channels is not supported by any measurement in Wwox tissue: the catalogue mechanism record lists T-type only, the source paper's own oocyte data show GIRK block near the labelled band (a GIRK route would predict the opposite sign; prior knowledge), the two PTZ-alone null cohorts of the figure differ by about the size of the drug effect, no interaction test, and P17 Cacna1g/h/Kcnj6 transcripts are inside the control-line background. The late-phase effect stays one experiment in one laboratory; the group is unchanged.

G1.label: Strongest WWOX-specific case today (in the mouse null)
G1.statement: a favourable result in a WWOX system, read against an untreated comparator of the same genotype from a full or partial text, with no position-blocking flag and no null, unfavourable or mixed WWOX-system result beside it (position F1); a reading-quality screen on the rows the position rests on (it may rest on a single row, which the item states), not a size of effect and not a result of recovery after onset

G2a.label: Favourable but thin WWOX-system readout, specificity not in question
G2a.statement: a favourable result in a WWOX system with reading or design limits only (uncontrolled, graphical, one experiment, depth-limited), no null beside it, and none of the specificity flags below (position F2)

G2b.label: Favourable but thin, specificity uncertain or untested
G2b.statement: as G2a, and the favourable readout carries a specificity flag: it also occurs in wild type, or it was obtained with a tool compound, or no drug-by-genotype test exists, or the wild-type arm is floor-limited (position F2 with a specificity flag). Not having tested specificity is an unknown, never a clean reading; G2a versus G2b is not an efficacy order

G3.label: Tried in a WWOX system: results mixed, null or case-level
G3.statement: favourable and null or unfavourable WWOX-system results side by side, or only a null one; the study is to learn which holds (positions C2, C1). The intervention is listed because it has been tried in a WWOX system, not because its favourable part is stronger than that of untried candidates; the class label of the unit describes the pertinence of the favourable part and is not a verdict

G4a.label: Target-based hypothesis, direction-consistent action documented
G4a.statement: no test of the intervention in a WWOX system; favourable support outside WWOX; the need has WWOX-system observations; a catalogue action coherent with the need's direction is documented (position F3). The documented action does not by itself support WWOX relevance: the need's WWOX observation may rest on a different intervention

G4b.label: Target-based hypothesis, direction not established
G4b.statement: as G4a but no documented direction-consistent action: the need's direction is uncertain, the action is unresolved, or the unit has no catalogue identity (position F3)

G5.label: Weak pertinence or counter-evidence outside WWOX
G5.statement: no signed WWOX-system result of the intervention and either a harm or null signal outside WWOX with nothing favourable beside it, or a link by mechanism only (positions C3, P3)

GU.label: Not yet orderable: premise missing
GU.statement: an abstention (a datum is missing before any test can be designed), no step named, or no linked need of this objective carries a position; NOT a finding that the unit is unpromising

direction_states.opposed_risk: a documented action of this intervention pushes against another need of the same objective
direction_states.resolved: the need states an up/down intervention direction
direction_states.unresolved: the need's own direction is uncertain: no lever on it can be qualified either way, which is a visible gap and not a negative finding

origin_classes.external_transferred: carried in from another condition or literature by a stated mechanistic analogy

investigations.plain_statement: An order of investigations to fund, not a ranking of efficacy: each row orders the value of the next discriminating experiment (what its result would change, at what cost), not a probability of benefit. The positions are curated judgements written by research agents and reviewed row by row; the code validates them and computes no position. An unresolved or opposed direction is named in the row's decisive uncertainty and the order does not imply a direction the evidence does not support. Nothing here is medical advice.
investigations.unit_of_a_row: a question on compound-action-context-benefit with one concrete next step; the same compound may appear in more than one row for different objectives or contexts
what_is_not_rewarded: number of linked pathways or needs
ease of purchase or access category
depth of existing evidence (carried separately as evidence_depth)

uncarded.item: ACK1 (TNK2) and ITCH as regulators of WWOX protein stability (Q1 complement): dasatinib and bosutinib as paired ACK1 probes, conditional on WWOX protein being present
uncarded.reason: Q1 complement (IT10 P2.3): Q1 has no graph route, and a complementary search for regulators of WWOX protein stability yields one usable slice, a mechanism experiment on protein level only. ACK1 over-expression with an engineered activated kinase phosphorylates WWOX, predominantly at Tyr287, and is followed by polyubiquitination, mostly in HEK293T cells (endogenous Wwox ubiquitination in LNCaP appears only after MG-132, and the ubiquitin assays are under MG-132 pretreatment); degradation as a consequence of Tyr287 phosphorylation is inferred, not shown (PMID 16288044, Mahajan 2005, full text read at the original on 2026-10-31, receipt FTR-20261031-16288044-01, Figs 1-8 inspected, supplement unavailable: phosphorylation and polyubiquitination are shown in overexpressed non-neural cells with an engineered activated kinase; Tyr287 is the predominant, not the only, phosphorylation site by pTyr signal; the paper does not show that Y287F resists ubiquitination or degradation, Fig 5E has no lane without activated Ack1 and one time point, Fig 5F shows MG-132-revealed ubiquitination and no level rescue so the proteasomal route is inferred, and no ACK1 inhibitor is measured against WWOX); ACK1 shRNA raised WWOX in one HCC line (MHCC-97H), one construct versus scrambled, steady state only (PMID 25738261, full text read 2026-10-30 in IT11 P2.4; it supports ONLY the direction 'knockdown raises WWOX', not the Tyr287 or ubiquitin route). Two catalogued ATP-site inhibitors with measured TNK2 potency (dasatinib, bosutinib; multi-target SRC/ABL kinase inhibitors that share SRC/ABL targets and bind SRC tighter than ACK1: concordance of the two does not identify ACK1 and bosutinib is not an independent chemotype; IT11 P2.4) would be paired probes with the concordance rule (agreement with TNK2 knockdown, a response to one only is off-target); the repeated ChEMBL values (bosutinib 2.7 nM, dasatinib Kd 5.6 and 6.0 nM) are literature values carried between papers, not replicates. CONDITIONAL on WWOX protein being present: no model is shown to have a variant protein above the assay floor, and a band not detected in the Q230P fibroblast blot does not separate a protein made and cleared from one never made, so the substrate is UNCONFIRMED, not excluded. Nothing predicts function; ITCH raises WWOX half-life but has no compound. COUNTER-EVIDENCE: the ACK1 observation is cancer-cell over-expression (prostate, liver); no Tyr287 change in serum-starved MEFs; MG-132 raised neither wild type nor the P252A or P282A constructs, so a proteasomal route is not shown in the only variant system, whereas chloroquine and NH4Cl restored P252A and chloroquine also prevented its degradation under cycloheximide (a main-text sentence of PMID 41124647), which supports a lysosomal route; ACK1 inhibition sensitised rat cerebellar granule neurons to apoptotic stress (PMID 37263460, abstract); broad kinase inhibitors shift WWOX phospho-forms in cancer cells. The TNK2 missense that abolishes NEDD4 binding in a family with infantile-onset epilepsy (PMID 23686771, abstract) is NOT counter-evidence for lowering ACK1: the abstract gives no kinase-activity direction and it is one family. CNS exposure and tolerability of both agents were not assessed. Not carded: R3 is satisfied as to the source (Mahajan 2005 and the HCC paper both read) and shows the decisive datum is absent from both, so the unit still waits for a datum that no source holds: a WWOX level, half-life or ubiquitination read after an ACK1-directed intervention including Tyr287Phe, with the no-activated-ACK1 arm and the route arm (ack1_it13_mahajan_20261031/controls_ack1_it13.tsv). Substrate census (IT12 P1-main, 2026-10-31; priority NOT raised, scope narrowed): in published neural WWOX models only wild-type cells (hESC/iPSC neural stem cells and organoids), AAV add-back (wild-type sequence) and one SCAR12 genotype (two siblings, each homozygous for ONE variant, c.1114G>C p.Gly372Arg, a C-terminal missense; its result does not extend to Q230P or to missense variants in general) show any band; the SCAR12 band is faint (0.1 to 0.3 of an unrelated wild type, one membrane) and on a second blot (EV6F, GAPDH loading control; the first blot EV1N uses HSP90) it is similar to the knockout lanes, so it is not shown above the assay floor; the WOREE lines show no visible band (EV1M, where wild-type band saturation is clear; it is mild in EV1N and EV6F). Q230P fibroblast blot: there is a negative control (CRISPR knockout clones) and three positive cancer/HEK lines, but no healthy fibroblast control and no heterozygote lane, and the epitope of the antibody sc-20528 is not stated. lde/lde rat: a trace frameshift product with a newer antibody (HPA050992, aa 32 to 110); that the earlier 'null' call depended on the antibody is the authors' hypothesis, not a demonstrated fact, and the paper gives 'lower mobility' in the Results but 'slightly heavier' in Discussion and legend (46.2 kDa; frameshift product predicted +0.8 kDa). Conclusion: no model has a protein level shown above the assay floor; the substrate for a stability lever is UNCONFIRMED, not excluded; the G372R line is the one model to retest first, after gate G0 (two antibodies, knockout floor). Q1 unit text: the reference class allele Q230P has no band in one non-neural line, no matched control, antibody sc-20528; made-and-cleared versus not made is open; the only neural lines with a missense allele are G372R (SCAR12) and G137V (WCH, iPSC only).

uncarded.item: Digoxin (cardiac glycoside; HIF1A-axis inhibitor in cells) on the null-mouse glycaemia readout
uncarded.reason: A candidate gap in the phenotype-first list: in the Wwox-null mouse digoxin raised blood glucose within 40 minutes (n=3, no wild-type arm attested; the printed dose of 100 mg/kg i.p. is flagged implausible), a readout the vector add-back also recovers longitudinally (glycaemia normal from P20, PMID 42422765). Same endpoint class, a different measure (acute versus longitudinal), systemic not neural, one source relayed from the repository census (PMC body empty on 2026-09-22), and digoxin acts through Na/K-ATPase with HIF1A inhibition as a side pharmacology. A cardiac glycoside is generally understood to have a narrow therapeutic window (general pharmacology, not checked here). Not a neural benefit and not a candidate; recorded so the gap in the phenotype-first list is visible.

uncarded.item: Kv7 (KCNQ2/3) openers: ezogabine as an ex vivo probe, azetukalner as the clinical-stage member
uncarded.reason: IT14 P3 re-labelled this proposal as the counter-hypothesis (refuter) arm of the inhibition question: the heterozygote shares the input-resistance change and is intermediate in resting potential yet bursts in 4 of 23 slices against 36 of 42, so a graded intrinsic change alone does not account for the difference in bursting unless a threshold effect is invoked (the 1.9 mV heterozygote-versus-knockout gap in resting potential was not tested). A proposal of IT13 P3a, not carded: the basis is a depolarised resting potential reported in a neuron-deleted slice study (about 5 mV, Breton 2021, relayed) and, weakly, Kcnq2/Kcnq3 transcripts lower in the P17 deposits; the Kcnq2 difference sits inside the control-line background (not interpretable at n of 2 to 4) and direction of a channel mRNA is not benefit. A reduced channel number lowers the ceiling of an opener. Identity from ChEMBL only (ezogabine CHEMBL41355 phase 4, KCNQ opener; azetukalner CHEMBL5095264 phase 3, no mechanism record in ChEMBL); ezogabine withdrawal and metabolite statements are prior knowledge and not verified here; paediatric exposure, label and safety were not searched. Ex vivo probe use only, development not assessed; no WWOX result exists for any Kv7 agent.
uncarded.what_would_reopen: resting potential and the XE991-sensitive current in knockout versus control neurons, then an opener effect on bursts with the bath composition stated (reopen trigger NP3A3)

uncarded.item: Benzodiazepine-site positive modulation of fast GABA-A inhibition: clobazam and its metabolite N-desmethylclobazam as ex vivo probes (compensation of a measured inhibitory loss)
uncarded.reason: A function-first probe-level hypothesis of IT14 P3, not carded. Generated by the largest knockout-specific effect stated in Breton 2021 (sIPSC amplitude about -52 percent in layer II/III pyramidal cells of the neuron-deleted neocortical slice); inferred: that the loss is receptor-limited rather than release-limited and that a potentiator can restore enough charge (the knockout amplitude is about 48 percent of control and in recombinant receptors the metabolite's maximal potentiation is 143 to 253 percent of the GABA response at EC10 in rat HEK293 cells and 203 to 270 percent at EC20 in human oocytes, readouts that are not directly comparable). Counter-evidence and limits: heterozygote-versus-wild-type inhibition is not reported and the heterozygote bursts in 4 of 23 slices; excitatory-gain and intrinsic (input resistance, sag) readings stay live; sIPSC was recorded with a KCl internal solution; subtype selectivity of both agents is disputed across three primary papers (efficacy ratio alpha2/alpha1 of the metabolite 1.77 in rat HEK293 cells, a comparison that confounds the alpha subtype with the beta subunit (alpha1beta2gamma2 against alpha2beta3gamma2); non-selective in human oocytes, modest alpha2 affinity preference in binding); no GABAergic drug has been tested in any WWOX preparation. Identity: ChEMBL CHEMBL70418 (clobazam) and CHEMBL2260842 (N-desmethylclobazam, listed as NOR-CLOBAZAM); label and exposure facts are not carried here; ex vivo probe use only, no systemic or paediatric claim and no dose.
uncarded.what_would_reopen: not a precondition for a class-level ex vivo arm; E0 locus data, heterozygote-versus-wild-type sIPSC data or a same-system subtype comparison change how a result is attributed (triggers NP3P1 to NP3P3)

uncarded.item: GluN2B negative allosteric modulators at the ifenprodil site (ifenprodil and Ro 25-6981 as tools, radiprodil as clinical-stage comparator) as ex vivo probes of the NMDAR contribution to slice bursting
uncarded.reason: IT15 Q-A target-first search (ChEMBL, graded same-document comparisons) with independent verification. Generated by the d-APV sensitivity of the neuron-deleted slice bursts together with the unmeasured NMDAR current. Pharmacology: GluN2B over GluN2A about 360-fold (ifenprodil, human, 3 uM glycine, -40 mV) and about 5,800-fold (Ro 25-6981, rat context), two independent papers compiled in a review with different stated conditions; the expected fall of the isolated current is an upper bound (incomplete inhibition, triheteromers); radiprodil has only complex-level values. Limits: the GluN2B share of the slice NMDAR current is unmeasured; pore blockers show no subunit selectivity detected; no GluN2B NAM was tested in any WWOX preparation; a steeper burst fall is not a valid discriminator alone. Ex vivo probe use only: no systemic, paediatric or dose statement.
uncarded.what_would_reopen: NP5A1 to NP5A3 (a measured GluN2B-sensitive share, a same-system comparison, assay context where it is missing)

uncarded.item: GSK3 inhibitors of different classes (ATP-site, irreversible non-ATP-competitive, ion-competitive) as tools to measure GSK3 output in WWOX loss
uncarded.reason: IT15 Q-B target-first search with independent verification: partial abstention. No compound is nominated. The premise is one pSer9 blot (one lane per genotype per region, no statistics); no kinase-activity assay exists in a WWOX system; lithium acted in all genotypes including wild type. Tool experiment proposed: kinase activity and Tau pS396/S404 against beta-catenin phospho and AXIN2/LEF1 for an ATP-site inhibitor, lithium and tideglusib, with an Axin-pathway control that itself needs GSK3. Corrected by the verifier: GSK3A/GSK3B ratio about 1 holds for the named compounds only (86 same-document pairs above 10-fold exist for others); substrate-competitive compounds exist in ChEMBL under other names; one qualitative document pairs Tau phospho with beta-catenin (not WWOX). Ex vivo tool use only; no therapeutic statement.
uncarded.what_would_reopen: NP5B1 to NP5B3 (an activity or substrate-phosphorylation readout, a genotype-by-inhibitor interaction, a quantitative paired readout)

counter: Rescue is not normalisation: unmyelinated axons per field remain about 52 versus about 26 in wild type.
The neuron-promoter vector corrected neuronal function without correcting radial-glia abnormalities (organoid arm); SATB2 mRNA overshoots wild type up to about eleven-fold in treated organoids.

No ceiling is measured and no tumour-surveillance or overexpression-toxicity endpoint exists in the mouse study; applied recombinant WWOX lowered viability of human ESC-derived cortical neurons in a preprint. More is not safer.
limit: G1 rests on a single pertinence row: high-dose survival, n=30 vs untreated knockout n=10, flag audit_repair_not_rejudged; the audit repair on that row is still to be adjudicated before any claim-level use. Prevention or early-window result in a null mouse (injection P0 to P5; later intervention not explored); one laboratory (two papers, shared senior author).

External precedent (not WWOX): seizure endpoints after onset are split by restoration mode and endpoint identity; myelin sheath structure after onset in a neuron-driven lesion is unmeasured; a post-onset null on spike-wave rate alone would be consistent with part of the precedent set and must not be pre-registered as expected.
note: Graph coverage (IT11 P2.1): gene addition is out of the method (a modality, not a molecule), so the graph is silent on it by construction; its WWOX-system result is not a graph result. The five phenotype leads are development inputs, not an independent validation.

notes: IT27: in the partial-loss P47T mouse (missense with protein present; prefrontal cortex, parietal cortex and hippocampus, ten animals, one origin) Chac1 is higher in all three regions (log2FC +0.58, +1.11, +1.25; padj 0.10, 0.0497, 0.30) and Trib3 is higher in parietal cortex and hippocampus (+0.80, +1.54) but not prefrontal cortex (-0.21); none of the Trib3 values is significant. It is a third, different perturbation, not a resolution of the human sign.

IT28 (CH-IT28-ISR-ROLE): the sign of an ISR lever depends on the node perturbed and on the stress class, and RNA target sets can disagree with eIF2-alpha phosphorylation in both directions, so no lever class (eIF2B activator, kinase inhibitor, potentiator) is preferable before the protein-level sign is measured by cell type.

counter: IT12 P2.2 figure audit (dated 2026-10-31, PMID 37275776 Fig 7B, image viewed): the stored statement that the GIRK2 crossings lie inside the therapeutic band is wrong on one clause. In oocytes the GIRK2 homomer activated by Gbeta-gamma is half-maximally inhibited at about 0.03 to 0.06 mM, about 4 to 8 times BELOW the shaded band (about 0.25 to 0.9 mM), while the brain-predominant GIRK1/2 plus Gbeta-gamma channel crosses at about 0.4 to 1 mM, inside it (partial block, about 20 to 60 percent). So a measured non-T-type target exists at labelled exposure, and the wording 'T-type potency is weak against the labelled range' is not the whole story: the ethosuximide result in the WWOX mouse (PTZ seizure score) cannot be attributed to T-type mediation. An oocyte datum, not a WWOX mechanism; the authors say neuronal GIRK2 homomer abundance is unknown. In a genetic absence model the relay-neuron T-type current is smaller than control and the burst-threshold difference follows Ih (PMID 24953239 Figs 5 and 6). No group or member evidence changes.

IT13 P3a (2026-10-31): ethosuximide's attribution to T-type channels is not supported by any measurement in Wwox tissue: the catalogue mechanism record lists T-type only, the source paper's own oocyte data show GIRK block near the labelled band (a GIRK route would predict the opposite sign; prior knowledge), the two PTZ-alone null cohorts of the figure differ by about the size of the drug effect, no interaction test, and P17 Cacna1g/h/Kcnj6 transcripts are inside the control-line background. The late-phase effect stays one experiment in one laboratory; the group is unchanged.
limit: same paper and laboratory as lithium (PMID 32000863), one experiment, i.p., one PTZ dose, effect confined to the late phase; no wild-type or drug-by-genotype test and the wild-type arm is floor-limited, so absence of a wild-type effect is unknown, not clean; the paper reports lithium better than ethosuximide

Counts in children are not independent exposures: the children counted for vigabatrin, hormonal therapy, the ketogenic diet and cannabidiol overlap across the four classes and across reports (three of the five vigabatrin children with both endpoints also supply other classes; all five had co-therapy), and some children may be double-counted across reports.

No published WWOX-DEE child has an instrumented, sustained response: a partial or transient improvement with development unchanged is not a sustained response, and an absent developmental gain is not proof that no benefit exists; developmental statements are clinical narratives without a scale.

Hormonal co-therapy is measured as a risk factor in the sibling cohort (the same group's 64-child vigabatrin cohort: concomitant prednisolone associated with the imaging abnormality, univariable, abstract level), and its status in the two WWOX-DEE children with the change is unknown, so it is a named confounder, not a neutral unknown; the frequency of the abnormality in selected cohorts is not attributable risk in WWOX.

Counts in children are not independent exposures: the children counted for vigabatrin, hormonal therapy, the ketogenic diet and cannabidiol overlap across the four classes and across reports (three of the five vigabatrin children with both endpoints also supply other classes; all five had co-therapy), and some children may be double-counted across reports.

No published WWOX-DEE child has an instrumented, sustained response: a partial or transient improvement with development unchanged is not a sustained response, and an absent developmental gain is not proof that no benefit exists; developmental statements are clinical narratives without a scale.

Hormonal co-therapy is measured as a risk factor in the sibling cohort (the same group's 64-child vigabatrin cohort: concomitant prednisolone associated with the imaging abnormality, univariable, abstract level), and its status in the two WWOX-DEE children with the change is unknown, so it is a named confounder, not a neutral unknown; the frequency of the abnormality in selected cohorts is not attributable risk in WWOX.

counter: A polyclonal human fibroblast WWOX pool shows LOWER cytoplasmic HIF-1alpha in two of four conditions and no nuclear difference on its own blot (one blot repetition shown; a different compartment from the mouse nuclear increase), although its HRE reporter, HIF1A mRNA, total HIF-1alpha and lactate go up; HIF1A mRNA is flat in both human neural transcript systems; mouse P17 brain shows no elevation of HIF-axis transcripts.

The engine edge HIF1A to BNIP3 is a review-sourced SIGNOR record on a complex; the primary record (Bruick 2000) is in non-neural cell lines; the HIF-prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor roxadustat raises HIF (whether that is the disease direction is open: direction conditional, H-protect) and its label lists seizures and secondary hypothyroidism, and thyromimetic action is from a 2025 paper, not the label.

Mouse P17 brain with Wwox deletion shows no elevation of HIF-axis or glycolysis transcripts in four contrasts (Hif1a flat, Epas1 and Slc2a1 lower): the in-vivo brain does not side with the organoid (bulk transcripts, epileptic lines, post hoc computation); the P47T knock-in brain reports hypoxia, apoptosis and glycolysis hallmark gene-set enrichment with no direction stated in the text.

IT12 P2-P47T (dated 2026-10-31; the set means were recomputed independently from the GEO counts): the adult P47T knock-in brain (partial loss, seizures, gliosis; 5 v 5 animals, transcripts only) shows a broad modest shift led by glycolytic enzyme transcripts and NOT the organoid's selective hypoxia-response pattern (selective six-gene set +0.22, +0.11, -0.07, +0.19 log2 in hippocampus, cortex, PFC, cerebellum; exact p 0.32, 0.70, 0.67, 0.057; the Adm rise is a two-animal effect). The K01 reopening condition is not met in substance (no HIF protein, activity or lactate datum). Decision: narrow and separate three hypotheses (H-org, H-act, H-glia); no strengthening, no change of step 0 or arms A to C, no priority change. The authors' hippocampal differential-expression sheet does not follow the deposit (cause unverifiable); the GSEA re-run is the producer's only.
limit: proposed, not performed. counter: NRF2 activation lowers Il6 and Il1b but leaves Tnf unchanged in stimulated bone-marrow macrophages (no microglia), so the engine edge NFE2L2 to TNF is contradicted by its primary paper; the null-hippocampus Tnf-a increase is not significant; early-passage Wwox-null MEFs already show raised redox transcripts (possible ceiling); brain NRF2 target induction by omaveloxolone in monkey is modest; CDDO-EA seizure precedent is a different molecule in adult rat with engagement not measured.
limit: proposed, not performed. No NRF2 pathway, ROS or cytokine-protein datum exists in any WWOX-deficient mammalian neural cell; every WWOX cytokine datum is a transcript (null hippocampus Il6 significant, Tnf-a not; P47T cerebellum IL1B and TNF; rat lde/lde glia lower; the human KO organoid has no cytokine-expressing cells).
